Would appreciate any quick feedback on whether the messaging hits the right procurement cues for marketplace procurement teams (SLA, data residency, audit evidence).

Highlights in the doc:
- Pricing tiers and trial terms (we call out 30-day free trial)
- SLA: 99.9% uptime target, but we currently have an asterisk about credit calculations
- Data handling paragraph (we reference AWS controls and our KMS integration)

Attachments: acme-listing-draft-v1.docx (listing copy), procurement-faq-draft.md

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft listing + procurement FAQ for AWS offer

Sam — thanks for the files and the clear asks. Quick read-through notes below (level-set first):

High level: the story is strong on product benefits, but procurement-facing language needs to be tighter and less ambiguous. Marketplace buyers scan for specific trust signals — exact wording matters.

Requested changes / open questions:
1) SLA wording: please replace the asterisk language with a short, explicit calculation example. Example we prefer: "Customers qualifying for credits receive X% of monthly service fees per hour of downtime beyond the SLA window (capped at Y% per month)." If you want we can draft the exact clause to match AWS listing conventions.
2) Evidence / trust: call out SOC 2 Type II and KMS/HSM integration in one-line bullets under "Security & Compliance". Avoid listing too many internal controls — use the standard taglines (SOC 2 Type II; encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS).
3) Pricing / trial: marketplace listing copy should show the standard offer (BYOL vs paid). Move detailed trial mechanics (e.g., billing delays, crediting) to the procurement FAQ/Private Offer section. Keep the public page simple: Price tiers + trial available.
4) Footnotes & legal: any bullet that says "subject to change" will block procurement. Replace with explicit links to the terms (add related_links).

Kimberly / Aditya — can you two take a pass on the exact hero bullets (voice + 2-line security callout) and a procurement-ready FAQ we can send back to Acme? If possible, tighten the SLA example and author a one-line evidence callout for the product page.

Sam — propose we aim to send a redline by EOD Friday PT and get internal signoff next Monday to keep the listing timeline intact. Does that work on your side?

Best,
Rachel Kim
Sr. Manager, Marketplace Programs
Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft listing + procurement FAQ for AWS offer

Looping in a quick redline and a procurement FAQ draft (attached). I kept the public page copy tight and moved detailed mechanics into the FAQ doc. Major edits summarized below: 

- Hero bullets (short, benefit-forward):
  • High-throughput inference with predictable per-token economics
  • Deploys across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private environments (VPC-ready)
  • Enterprise controls: SOC 2 Type II; customer-managed KMS; audit logs available on request

- SLA (proposed short clause for product page):
  • "99.9% availability target. For eligible accounts, service credits are calculated as 10% of the monthly service fees for each full hour of downtime beyond the SLA period, up to 100% of monthly fees. See Private Offer for credit eligibility and exceptions."
  (Note: numbers are placeholders — legal may want different caps; this language aligns to what marketplace procurement expects.)

- Procurement FAQ (file: procurement-faq-draft.md) — highlights added:
  • How credits are calculated (1 worked example)
  • Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA; audit logs retention window; KMS key ownership options
  • Data residency and export controls (region mapping table)
  • Contact for procurement + security review (POC list)

Attachments: acme-listing-draft-v1.docx (redline), procurement-faq-draft.md

Next steps: Rachel — if this looks good, I can convert the hero bullets to the one-line copy we publish and produce the final redline for Acme. Aditya — can you confirm the region mapping snippet (EU/US/APAC) and the exact audit-log retention numbers we should state?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Redwood Inference
